actions.action: Check that the top inch of soil is dry before watering
Slide the plant out of the pot and inspect the roots
If the roots are mushy, black or smelly, trim them with clean scissors
Repot into fresh, well-draining mix (peat-based with perlite, or orchid/bark mix)
Check for a drainage hole; if there is none, use a draining pot or put a plastic nursery pot inside the planter
Water thoroughly until it drains, then empty the saucer
Place in bright, indirect light away from harsh sun, heaters and drafts
Take 2–3-segment cuttings and plant them in a small pot of moist mix as a backup

reason: The answer correctly identifies dehydration with old, compacted soil, and its main advice (repot into fresh mix, then water when dry) matches the fix the poster used; the advice to wait before watering depends on checking the soil, so it is not harmful.
